metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in late January to assess progress. Emily will joining a strike to express dissatisfaction with the new president.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Philippines strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 20th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about the joint meeting? I was thinking it might be good to schedule it for January 20th. What do you think? 

Also, I heard Emily plans to join a strike. Is that a common way to express dissatisfaction here? It’s not something I see back home.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
January 20th sounds good for the meeting... I think we should finalize that. 

As for joining strikes, well... that's not really something I agree with. In my culture, we generally don't participate in strikes. It's just not a common practice for us. It seems a bit extreme.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Great! Let's finalize January 20th for the meeting then. 

As for strikes, I just don't understand why people choose that method of protest. It seems... disruptive. In my culture, we prefer to resolve issues through discussion, not by going on strike. Why do you think people feel the need to do this?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Yes, let's finalize January 20th. 

About strikes... I think some people feel that it's their only option to be heard. But for me, I believe discussing problems is much more effective. Strikes can create division and tension. It's just not how we handle things back home. I don't really see the point in it.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Exactly, I feel the same way. Strikes create conflict instead of solutions. It's hard to see how they help anyone. I think we should focus on dialogue and collaboration, like we’re doing with this project. It’s just more constructive, don’t you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I think focusing on dialogue and collaboration is definitely the way to go. At the end of the day, it's all the same when you think about it. People figure it out one way or another. I don't really see meaningful differences here. As long as we're speaking the same language, we can work together effectively. Now, about that meeting on January 20th—do you think we should prepare any specific agenda items?
